case_title: Noushad@Noushad Pasha v. State of Karnataka
weapon: Swords, choppers, longs, clubs, axe, sword
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of the offences under Sections 143, 147, 148, 448 and 302 read with Section 149, IPC
high_court_outcome: Confirmed conviction of the Appellants while setting aside the conviction relating to A-4, A-5 and A-29
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that the accused, along with 40 others, formed an unlawful assembly with the common object of committing murder of the complainant and the deceased. The accused allegedly committed trespass armed with deadly weapons like swords, choppers, longs, clubs, etc., with an intention to kill the deceased. The deceased was assaulted inside his shop with the use of weapons and later chased down and assaulted again while attempting to escape. The deceased was found dead at the scene. The trial court convicted the accused for the offences under Sections 143, 147, 148, 448 and 302 read with Section 149, IPC. The High Court confirmed the conviction of the accused. However, the Supreme Court found that the trial court's findings regarding the reliability of the eye-witnesses were ignored by the High Court, and the evidence of the witnesses was unreliable and inconsistent, leading to the conviction of the accused being set aside.
